text:
Evgeni Malkin is 40, in his 21st season with the Penguins, and the trade speculation around a struggling Pittsburgh team has inevitably reached him. Daily Faceoff asked what happens to him if the Penguins sell, Wild and Canucks outlets have run the hypotheticals, and NDTV Sports reported this week that he's expected to stay. For now he's still producing: 17 points in 17 games, 12 in his last ten.

The production is honest. He has 6 goals on 4.7 expected, Pittsburgh's on-ice luck with him is modest, and his scoring rate sits inside the range our numbers expect. The Penguins control 55% of five-on-five expected goals with him out there. His minutes have dipped over his last ten games, to under 17 a night, which is the one number worth tracking at his age.

Last season showed the full trade-off. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among forwards for creating expected goals and the bottom 4% for what he gave up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush, a 40-year-old still living in transition. Whatever Pittsburgh decides, he's still the kind of center who makes a power play better.
headline: Malkin at 40, in a season of rumors
